mstts:express-as.prosody:
Welcome—I'm so glad you're here. Have you ever wondered why so much of our self-worth seems tied to how we look, or how much we’re liked? Together, we're about to take a fresh look at those old rules and silent expectations—especially the ones that shape how women see themselves and their place in the world.
Inspired by Florence Given’s bold voice in Women Don't Owe You Pretty, this journey asks us to pause and really think. Who sets the standards for beauty and approval anyway—and who actually benefits from them? As we explore these questions, we'll uncover the hidden forces behind validation, people-pleasing, and those subtle pressures that tug at identity and relationships. But it’s not just about pointing out what’s wrong. We’re here to find out what it means to reclaim your voice, set boundaries, and decide—once and for all—that you are enough, just as you are. Florence Given’s perspective invites us to step away from self-doubt and into a space where self-acceptance isn’t just possible—it’s powerful. So, as we move forward together, get ready to challenge old beliefs, reflect on your own journey, and imagine what life could be like when you get to define your worth on your own terms. Let’s dive in—and start rewriting the story.
